verses.original: Μὴ κρίνετε ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε
verses.transliteration: Mē krinete hina mē krithēte
verses.literal: Do not judge or . . . you will be judged

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: en hō gar krimati krinete krithēsesthe kai en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin
verses.literal: For with the same judgment you pronounce you will be judged and with the measure you use it will be measured to you

verses.original: Τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς
verses.transliteration: Ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou tēn de en tō sō ophthalmō dokon ou katanoeis
verses.literal: Why do you look at the speck in - your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye

verses.original: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ
verses.transliteration: ē pōs ereis tō adelphō sou Aphes ekbalō to karphos ek tou ophthalmou sou kai idou hē dokos en tō ophthalmō sou
verses.literal: How can you say to your brother Let me take the speck out of your eye while there is still a beam in your own eye

verses.original: ὑποκριτά ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου
verses.transliteration: hypokrita ekbale prōton ek tou ophthalmou sou tēn dokon kai tote diablepseis ekbalein to karphos ek tou ophthalmou tou adelphou sou
verses.literal: You hypocrite First take the beam out of your own eye and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from - your brother’s eye

verses.original: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων μή‿ ποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: Mē dōte to hagion tois kysin mēde balēte tous margaritas hymōn emprosthen tōn choirōn mē pote katapatēsousin autous en tois posin autōn kai straphentes rhēxōsin hymas
verses.literal: Do not give dogs what is holy do not throw your pearls before swine If you do . . . they may trample them under their feet and then turn and tear you to pieces . . .

verses.original: Αἰτεῖτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν ζητεῖτε καὶ εὑρήσετε κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Aiteite kai dothēsetai hymin zēteite kai heurēsete krouete kai anoigēsetai hymin
verses.literal: Ask and it will be given to you seek and you will find knock and the door will be opened to you

verses.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται
verses.transliteration: pas gar ho aitōn lambanei kai ho zētōn heuriskei kai tō krouonti anoigēsetai
verses.literal: For everyone who asks receives he who seeks finds and to him who knocks the door will be opened

verses.original: Ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Ē tis estin ex hymōn anthrōpos hon aitēsei ho huios autou arton mē lithon epidōsei autō
verses.literal: Which . . . of you if his . . . . . . son asks for bread will give . . . him a stone

verses.original: ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: ē kai ichthyn aitēsei mē ophin epidōsei autō
verses.literal: Or if he asks for a fish will give . . . him a snake

verses.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: ei oun hymeis ponēroi ontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois hymōn posō mallon ho Patēr hymōn ho en tois ouranois dōsei agatha tois aitousin auton
verses.literal: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him

verses.original: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται
verses.transliteration: Panta oun hosa ean thelēte hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi houtōs kai hymeis poieite autois houtos gar estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai
verses.literal: In everything . . . . . . then do to others as . . . you would have them do . . . . . . to you For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets

verses.original: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι’ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs hoti plateia hē pylē kai eurychōros hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn apōleian kai polloi eisin hoi eiserchomenoi di’ autēs
verses.literal: Enter through the narrow gate For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction and many - enter through it

verses.original: ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: hoti stenē hē pylē kai tethlimmenē hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn zōēn kai oligoi eisin hoi heuriskontes autēn
verses.literal: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life and only a few - find it

verses.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασιν προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες
verses.transliteration: Prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn hoitines erchontai pros hymas en endymasin probatōn esōthen de eisin lykoi harpages
verses.literal: Beware of false prophets They come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly they are ravenous wolves

verses.original: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα
verses.transliteration: apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous mēti syllegousin apo akanthōn staphylas ē apo tribolōn syka
verses.literal: By their fruit you will recognize them Are grapes gathered . . . from thornbushes or figs from thistles

verses.original: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ
verses.transliteration: houtōs pan dendron agathon karpous kalous poiei to de sapron dendron karpous ponērous poiei
verses.literal: Likewise every good tree bears good fruit but a bad tree bears bad fruit

verses.original: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν
verses.transliteration: ou dynatai dendron agathon karpous ponērous poiein oude dendron sapron karpous kalous poiein
verses.literal: A good tree cannot . . . bear bad fruit and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit

verses.original: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται
verses.transliteration: pan dendron mē poioun karpon kalon ekkoptetai kai eis pyr balletai
verses.literal: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire

verses.original: ἄρα¦γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: ara¦ge apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous
verses.literal: So then by their fruit you will recognize them

verses.original: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι Κύριε Κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀλλ’ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: Ou pas ho legōn moi Kyrie Kyrie eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn all’ ho poiōn to thelēma tou Patros mou tou en tois ouranois
verses.literal: Not everyone who says to Me Lord Lord will enter . . . the kingdom of heaven but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven

verses.original: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ Κύριε Κύριε οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν
verses.transliteration: polloi erousin moi en ekeinē tē hēmera Kyrie Kyrie ou tō sō onomati eprophēteusamen kai tō sō onomati daimonia exebalomen kai tō sō onomati dynameis pollas epoiēsamen
verses.literal: Many will say to Me on that day Lord Lord did we not prophesy . . . in Your name and in Your name drive out demons and - perform many miracles

verses.original: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν
verses.transliteration: kai tote homologēsō autois hoti Oudepote egnōn hymas apochōreite ap’ emou hoi ergazomenoi tēn anomian
verses.literal: Then I will tell them plainly . . . I never knew . . . you depart from Me you workers of lawlessness

verses.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν
verses.transliteration: Pas oun hostis akouei mou tous logous toutous kai poiei autous homoiōthēsetai andri phronimō hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn petran
verses.literal: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock

verses.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν
verses.transliteration: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosepesan tē oikia ekeinē kai ouk epesen tethemeliōto gar epi tēn petran
verses.literal: The rain fell the torrents raged and the winds blew and beat against that house yet it did not fall . . . because its foundation was on the rock

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον
verses.transliteration: kai pas ho akouōn mou tous logous toutous kai mē poiōn autous homoiōthēsetai andri mōrō hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn ammon
verses.literal: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand

verses.original: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἔπεσεν καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη
verses.transliteration: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosekopsan tē oikia ekeinē kai epesen kai ēn hē ptōsis autēs megalē
verses.literal: The rain fell the torrents raged and the winds blew and beat against that house and it fell and great was its collapse

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tous logous toutous exeplēssonto hoi ochloi epi tē didachē autou
verses.literal: When Jesus had finished saying these things the crowds were astonished at His teaching

verses.original: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: ēn gar didaskōn autous hōs exousian echōn kai ouch hōs hoi grammateis autōn
verses.literal: because He taught as one who had authority and not as their scribes
